title: api: unify rate-limit semantics, idempotency keys, and Retry-After across streaming and OpenAI-compat endpoints
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Users integrating Redwood via both native and OpenAI-compat APIs observed inconsistent rate-limit headers, differing error codes for retryable failures, and unreliable idempotency handling for streaming/long-poll requests. This PR unifies rate limit semantics and Retry-After behavior across the native and OpenAI-compat surfaces, hardens idempotency handling for streaming and function-calling requests, and standardizes error codes returned by the compatibility layer. Summary of changes: 1) Standardize headers: all endpoints now emit X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch seconds) and Retry-After (seconds) for both native and compatibility APIs. 2) Retry-After semantics: when a request is throttled due to per-key qps or burst limits, server returns 429 with Retry-After set to the number of seconds until the next allowed token burst. For enforcement at per-route vs per-account granularity the header reflects the strictest applicable limit. 3) Idempotency: introduce streaming-aware idempotency scope and TTLs. Idempotency-Key is accepted on streaming/create requests and function-call streams; semantics: 1) Non-idempotent requests (without key) behave as before. 2) With key, the first request creates a canonical response record. Retries within TTL (default 24h) will either return the cached final response for completed runs or attach the retry to the existing in-flight execution when safe. 3) For partial streaming responses we now store stream checkpoints (KV-mapped offsets) so retries can resume when backend supports it; otherwise we return a 409 with Retry-After to avoid conflicting side-effects. 4) Error codes: compatibility adapter previously returned 500 for many throttles; adapter now maps internal codes to stable OpenAI-like codes: 429 (rate_limit_exceeded), 503 (service_unavailable), 409 (conflict), 422 (invalid_request), 401 (authentication_error). 5) Streaming stability: fixed race in stream_manager where a slow consumer could cause in-memory idempotency lease to be dropped prematurely — now leases extend on active client ACKs and on outgoing chunk writes. 6) Observability: added rate-limit telemetry and idempotency hit/miss counters; new dashboards and alerting rules. 7) Backwards compatible: default behavior preserves existing clients but improves compatibility for OpenAI-compat consumers by returning consistent headers and codes. Migration notes: clients using the compatibility layer should stop relying on previous Retry-After formats and transition to integer-second Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* headers. Clients that use aggressive retry loops should add handling for 409 + Retry-After for streaming resumption. Testing: unit tests for header generation and idempotency store, integration e2e test exercising a streamed function-call with idempotency key, chaos test where backend rejects partial commit. Related: linear ENG-1429, ENG-1982, PM-312.
commits: init: implement header normalization and exporter for X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After
feat(idempotency): streaming-aware idempotency store with checkpointing and TTLs
fix(streaming): extend idempotency lease while client ACKs to avoid premature collision
chore(compat): map internal errors to OpenAI-compatible error codes and messages
test: add unit + integration tests for throttling paths and streaming retries
docs: document header semantics and migration guide
release_notes: - Standardize rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-*) and Retry-After (seconds) across native and OpenAI-compat endpoints. - Add streaming-aware idempotency support with checkpointing and TTL. - Map compatibility-layer errors to stable OpenAI-like error codes. - Improved streaming stability (lease extension on ACKs). - New telemetry and docs for migration.
review_comments: Ethan Chen: Overall looks good; two concerns: 1) can we guarantee TTL cleanup won't leak memory under an extreme number of unique keys? 2) confirm mapping of 500->429 only happens for throttles and not for transient infra failures.

Maya Patel: For TTL cleanup we batch expired-key sweeps and rely on the existing tombstone compaction job; added a configuration knob idempotency.cleanup.batch_size (default 1000) and documented it. Regarding mapping: adapter maps only explicitly-annotated throttle errors (ErrQuotaExceeded/ErrBurstExceeded) to 429; all other upstream 5xx remain 5xx. Added unit tests to assert mappings.

Priya Kapoor: Integration test failed earlier when e2e streaming test hit a race; I reproduced locally and pushed a fix to stream_manager to extend leases on chunk writes. Please run the streaming chaos test before merge.
Liam O'Connor: Minor nits on error message wording in docs and a suggestion to add a short migration snippet to SDKs.
notes: Follow-up work: backfill historical idempotency metrics (ENG-2154), add adaptive Retry-After calculation for multi-tenant burst sharing, and migrate SDKs to expose X-RateLimit helpers (tracked in ENG-2210).
